clue.text: One Tibetan animal in rite cooked as food

indicators.note: in tells us the animal goes inside the rearranged letters
something cooked has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the yak is the shaggy ox of Tibet

explanation.surface: A Tibetan ritual sees an animal sacrificed and cooked as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like part of the food picture but is the anagram signal; the shuffled letters are split by the animal just before their final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed in a sweet soy marinade, so it is a food.

clue.text: Building workers dividing opinion

indicators.note: dividing means the workers split the opinion in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a tenet is a belief or opinion held as true
men is a common crossword word for workers or staff

explanation.surface: A building's workforce is split over some question.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, so it is a kind of building.

clue.text: Born among wolves perhaps raised round bone

indicators.note: among says the birth word sits within the wolves' group
round says the reversed group wraps around the birth word
raised means lifted up, so in this down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: wolves run in a pack, the perhaps marking an example
née, meaning born, is used before a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A baby born among wolves is raised by them, a feral-child tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reads as brought up, the feral child's story, but in a down clue it means read upwards; 'among' and 'round' both signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap, or patella, is the small bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Barking setter shows the way

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter dog barks to show its owner which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the dog's noise but is the anagram signal, slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road or thoroughfare, as in 'the way' in a place name.

clue.text: Most important border in China

indicators.note: in says the border goes inside the friend

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a pal
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A news line about the key frontier region in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means first or fundamental, hence chief in rank or importance.

clue.text: Extraordinary pattern designed with a ruler

indicators.note: designed suggests these letters are drawn up afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remarkable pattern drawn using a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Preternatural means beyond what is normal or natural, so remarkable or exceptional.

clue.text: Confuses group stopping for each riverboat

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces fill the middle of the word for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
addles means muddles or confuses
a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: A confusing gang halts at each stop of a river cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steam-driven vessel with paddle wheels, typical on rivers such as the Mississippi.

clue.text: Lovers rapidly besmirched cabinet minister

indicators.note: besmirched means sullied or messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister's reputation is quickly ruined by a lovers' scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the UK's ancient government offices, now usually a sinecure held by a cabinet member.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this office, keeper of the monarch's private seal, sits in the British Cabinet as a senior minister.

clue.text: Dig a grave Mike must occupy

indicators.note: must occupy means the letter has to sit inside the serious word

parts.note: grave means serious or dire
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike must dig a grave and fill it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like spadework but is the slang verb for liking something.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to dig something is to like or appreciate it, a synonym of admire.

clue.text: Reverend in eastern capital around always

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole build is read backwards
in puts the clergy title inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A vicar in an eastern capital who has been around for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives EROMREVE (E + ROM, REV, E), and 'around' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means for all time, a poetic synonym of forever.

clue.text: Old woman cold in raincoat

parts.note: old woman is slang for mother, ma
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A cold old lady wrapped in her raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac is short for mackintosh, a waterproof coat.

clue.text: Delight as property initially let

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word property

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A landlord is delighted when the property is let at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to delight or gratify them.

clue.text: Open late — that's for making quick buck!

indicators.note: making here means making something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop owner opens late to make some fast money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick buck' reads as easy money, but the buck is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male deer or similar beast, and these swift horned grazers of Africa are famous for speed.

clue.text: Extremely long time inside after assault

indicators.note: inside means the letters are found within the run of words after assault

explanation.surface: A long stint in jail follows an assault conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, an age.

clue.text: Helps plucky players missing their intro?

indicators.note: missing their intro means the musicians lose their opening letter

parts.note: bass guitarists pluck their strings, so they are plucky players

explanation.surface: Brave players are given a hand when they fluff the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucky' means brave on the surface but here means plucking strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, so assists means helps.

clue.text: Runner outside unable to finish

indicators.note: unable to finish means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: skin is the outside surface of a body or fruit

explanation.surface: A runner on the outside lane fails to finish the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but a runner is also the blade a sledge slides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long runner fixed to boots for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Greek breaking link displays annoyance

indicators.note: breaking means splitting into the word for link from inside

parts.note: a chain is a series of links, or a link itself

explanation.surface: A Greek man is annoyed when a link breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance at failure or humiliation.

clue.text: House with male, 12, in mother country

parts.note: 12 points to the answer at 12 across, and the eland is a large African one of those

explanation.surface: A house shared with a male companion in the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference means an example of the 12-across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One's homeland is one's native land, the mother country.

clue.text: Road system turning to north in grubby outskirts?

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the outer letters
outskirts means only the outer letters of the word grubby are used
to north means heading upwards, so in this down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: rotary means turning or revolving

explanation.surface: A road system turns north through a seedy suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to north' means read upwards; 'turning' is the word reversed, not a second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyratory is a British one-way traffic system circling a block, like a large roundabout.

clue.text: Science needing a balanced approach?

parts.note: this branch of mechanics studies bodies at rest, where forces are balanced, so it literally needs balance

explanation.surface: A field of study that needs a level-headed method.
explanation.definitionFit: This physics branch deals with forces in equilibrium on bodies at rest.

clue.text: Embarrassed soldier capturing GI gets star

indicators.note: capturing means holding the American soldier inside the other pieces

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
a soldier is a caste of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A red-faced soldier who takes an American GI prisoner wins a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star such as Betelgeuse.

clue.text: Head from frozen residence, heavens overcast

indicators.note: head from means the first letter is taken away from the snowy house

parts.note: an igloo is an Inuit house built of snow
my and heavens are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A dark, cloudy sky above a snow house.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy weather is dark and dull, as when skies are overcast.

clue.text: Moles found in American facilities

parts.note: the gents is the men's toilet, and facilities is a euphemism for toilets

explanation.surface: Burrowing animals turn up in American bathrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moles' looks like burrowing animals but means spies; 'gents' is British slang for a men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, a kind of secret agent.

clue.text: Victim tense in Mary Rose at the front

indicators.note: in puts the tense letter inside the name Mary

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: at the front picks out the first letter of Rose

explanation.surface: A victim is found in the wreck of the Mary Rose, Henry VIII's sunken warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Rose was a Tudor warship that sank in 1545 and was raised in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who suffers or dies for a cause, so a victim.

clue.text: Beer: Guinness served shortly?

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the actor's first name loses its last letter

parts.note: Sir Alec Guinness was the British actor famous as Obi-Wan Kenobi

explanation.surface: A pint of Guinness, the Irish stout, served in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guinness' looks like the stout, but it is the actor Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: With river coming in, the setter's shelter is inadequate

indicators.note: coming in means the river enters between the other two pieces

parts.note: the setter's means the setter is, I'm
a tent is a portable shelter
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: The setter laments that a shelter is useless once a river floods in.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means powerless or ineffective, hence inadequate.

clue.text: Permissive character?

parts.note: read as a person who lets others do things, a permitter; read again as a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A description of someone easygoing about rules.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lets is someone who allows, and an alphabet character such as A or B has the same name.

clue.text: Gizmo needs electron motor reset

indicators.note: reset means set again in a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget that needs its electron motor resetting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gizmo is a gadget, and a TV handset that works the set from afar is a typical one.
